lectures.title: Mishlei 11:2 - Mishleic Tznius
lectures.description:
בָּא זָדוֹן וַיָּבֹא קָלוֹן וְאֶת צְנוּעִים חׇכְמָה:

This evening (11/1/21), in our Monday Night Mishlei Shiur, we learned Mishlei's take on tznius (modesty) and its relationship with chochmah. The pasuk was difficult in that it was quite vague - yet, we were able to come up with a good four or five solid ideas. I don't think it's an exaggeration to say that Mishlei's concept of tznius might evolve your view of tznius in general. But you can be the judge of that.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 22:14 - The Pitfall of the Strange Woman's Rhetoric (Part 2)
lectures.description: This morning (9/8/22), in our morning Mishlei shiur, we began by reviewing yesterday's pasuk, dividing it into three clear readings, and then attempting to uncover an idea from each. We developed an idea about the literal reading (i.e. that it's talking about an actual woman) based on Rabbeinu Yonah, and rushed through an idea about the allegorical reading (i.e. that it's talking about heretical philosophy) based on Metzudas David and Malbim, but we didn't have time to get to the third approach. There's a possibility we'll spend a third day on this, but most likely, we'll do Q&A tomorrow.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 22:14 - The Pitfall of the Strange Woman's Rhetoric (Part 1)
lectures.description:
שׁוּחָה עֲמֻקָּה פִּי זָרוֹת, זְעוּם י"י [יִפׇּל] (יפול) שָׁם:

This morning (9/7/22), in our morning Mishlei shiur, we picked up where we left off last year. Today's pasuk contains at least one mashal, if not two. Our time was a little cut short, due to our dwelling on some methodology points and due to our limited Zoom account, but we still managed to suggest a few approaches. Tomorrow we'll turn to the meforshim.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 22:3 - The Opposite of Seeing Evil and Hiding (Part 2)
lectures.description:
עָרוּם רָאָה רָעָה [וְנִסְתָּר] (ויסתר) וּפְתָיִים עָבְרוּ וְנֶעֱנָשׁוּ:

This morning (5/5/22), in our Morning Mishlei shiur, we continued working on our pasuk from yesterday and we came up with three (or four, depending on who you ask) nice ideas! More importantly, we emerged with a greater understanding of and appreciation for the Mishleic personality of the arum.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 22:3 - The Opposite of Seeing Evil and Hiding (Part 1)
lectures.description:
עָרוּם רָאָה רָעָה [וְנִסְתָּר] (ויסתר) וּפְתָיִים עָבְרוּ וְנֶעֱנָשׁוּ:

This morning (5/4/22), in our Morning Mishlei shiur, we began a rather tricky pasuk. Lots of questions and ambiguity. We made a few moves and discussed some nice methodology, but we're going to need to work on the pasuk some more on our own tomorrow (בג"ה) before we consult the meforshim.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 22:2 - Hashem Makes the Rich and the Poor (Part 2)
lectures.description:
עָשִׁיר וָרָשׁ נִפְגָּשׁוּ עֹשֵׂה כֻלָּם יי:

This morning (5/3/22), in our Morning Mishlei shiur, we continued our analysis of yesterday's pasuk, and learned through not one, not two, but SIX meforshim! We didn't manage to define how each one was learning the pasuk, but gleaned a little bit from all of them to sharpen our own ideas and to gain insights from their approaches. We also coined a new set of methodology terms: the "buffet approach" and the "salad bar" approach.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 22:2 - Hashem Makes the Rich and the Poor (Part 1)
lectures.description:
עָשִׁיר וָרָשׁ נִפְגָּשׁוּ עֹשֵׂה כֻלָּם יי:

This morning (4/29/22), in our Morning Mishlei shiur (which was slightly shorter than usual, due to Rosh Chodesh davening), we began learning a pasuk whose translation, questions, and problems were quite clear. We developed several fruitful approaches, one of which was Saadia Gaon's. Tomorrow we'll see what the other meforshim have to say (בג"ה).
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 11:18 - False Deeds and True Seeds
lectures.description:
רָשָׁע עֹשֶׂה פְעֻלַּת שָׁקֶר וְזֹרֵעַ צְדָקָה שֶׂכֶר אֱמֶת:

This evening (5/2/22), in our Monday Night Mishlei Shiur, we learned another pasuk about reshaim and tzadikim ... or at least, those who do tzedakah. The questions we came up with pointed us in some clear directions, and we were able to come up with several approaches of our own - one of which was echoed by Rabbeinu Yonah. We also learned Saadia Gaon's commentary, which ended up being very "meta."
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 22:1 - A Good Name is Preferable to Wealth (Part 2)
lectures.description:
This morning (4/29/22), in our Morning Mishlei shiur, we revisited the pasuk we learned yesterday. In contrast to yesterday, not only did we come up with several ideas on our own, but we also learned some ideas from the meforshim!

Note: towards the end of this shiur, I was in the middle of explaining an idea, when some aniyim came in. I nodded to one of the dorm guys to take care of the tzedakah distribution, and he indicated that he didn't want to interrupt the flow of the idea. I said some words (which you'll hear) and got up to give tzedakah myself. The dorm guy in question immediately regretted his decision, and went to give them tzedakah as well. I paused the recording, and when we resumed, I went over an idea from Mishlei about how interrupting our activities to give tzedakah is a virtue. Afterwards, I asked if we can keep this part of the recording intact, and the dorm guy agreed (because he recognized the value of the "Mishlei moment"), on the condition that I include an explanation of what happened, and made sure to point out that he usually DOES immediately respond to the needs of the aniyim, but was just so caught up in our learning that he wasn't thinking.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 21:30-31 - You Can't Outsmart Hashem (Part 2)
lectures.description:
Mishlei 21:30-31 - You Can't Outsmart Hashem (Part 2)

אֵין חׇכְמָה וְאֵין תְּבוּנָה וְאֵין עֵצָה לְנֶגֶד יְיָ:
סוּס מוּכָן לְיוֹם מִלְחָמָה וְלַיְיָ הַתְּשׁוּעָה:

This morning (4/7/22), in our Morning Mishlei shiur, we began by reviewing yesterday's pasuk and learning Saadia Gaon's commentary which generously furnished us with five interpretations! We then learned the final pasuk in the perek, which most meforshim learn in concert with the previous pasuk. We came up with our own approach, complemented by several meforshim. Our Morning Mishlei shiur will be on hiatus until sometime during the week after Pesach.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 21:30-31 - You Can't Outsmart Hashem (Part 1)
lectures.description:
Mishlei 21:30 - You Can't Outsmart Hashem

אֵין חׇכְמָה וְאֵין תְּבוּנָה וְאֵין עֵצָה לְנֶגֶד יְיָ:

This morning (4/6/22), in our Morning Mishlei shiur, we began learning a pasuk which we knew would be either very straightforward or very technical. It ended up being the former. We learned several different but related approaches on this pasuk as a standalone. The plan for tomorrow (בג"ה) is to learn the next pasuk as a standalone, and then learn the meforshim who take the two pesukim together.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 21:29 - The Visible Brazenness of the Rasha (Part 2)
lectures.description:
Mishlei 21:29 - The Visible Brazenness of the Rasha (Part 2)

הֵעֵז אִישׁ רָשָׁע בְּפָנָיו וְיָשָׁר הוּא [יָבִין] (יכין) [דַּרְכּוֹ] (דרכיו):

This morning (4/5/22), in our Morning Mishlei shiur, we continued our analysis of yesterday's pasuk. After reviewing our explanation of Saadia Gaon yesterday, we learned two more approaches: that of the Metzudos, who learns this to be a pasuk about anger, and that of the Rid and Rabbeinu Yonah who learn this to be about how reshaim lie. We concluded with Rabbeinu Yonah's commentary on how the last few pesukim are sequenced, which we didn't fully grasp, but derived a methodology principle therefrom nonetheless.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 21:29 - The Visible Brazenness of the Rasha (Part 1)
lectures.description:
Mishlei 21:29 - The Visible Brazenness of the Rasha (Part 1)

הֵעֵז אִישׁ רָשָׁע בְּפָנָיו וְיָשָׁר הוּא [יָבִין] (יכין) [דַּרְכּוֹ] (דרכיו):

This morning (4/4/22), in our Morning Mishlei shiur, we began a new pasuk which seems to be about how to read reshaim. After a brief intro about kre/ksiv in Tanach, we analyzed the pasuk and arrived at one complete approach. Tomorrow we'll learn the meforshim (בג"ה).
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 11:17 - Mishlei on Kindness and Cruelty
lectures.description:
גֹּמֵל נַפְשׁוֹ אִישׁ חָסֶד וְעֹכֵר שְׁאֵרוֹ אַכְזָרִי:

Last night (4/4/22), in our Monday Night Mishlei Shiur, we learned one of the few pesukim in Sefer Mishlei about chesed. This one was a real doozy to translate! Thankfully, we came up with six or seven of our own approaches to the pasuk and as many in the meforshim. There is still a lot more to be said here, especially if we take our pasuk to be teaching Mishlei's fundamental stance on chesed.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 21:28 - The Fate of the Lying Witness (Part 2)
lectures.description:
עֵד כְּזָבִים יֹאבֵד וְאִישׁ שׁוֹמֵעַ לָנֶצַח יְדַבֵּר:

This morning (3/31/22), in our Morning Mishlei shiur, we continued our analysis of yesterday's pasuk. After refining our understanding of Metzudas David, we learned Rabbeinu Yonah's approach, followed by the Meiri's derech nigleh and derech nistar approaches. This ended up being quite a fruitful pasuk!
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 21:28 - The Fate of the Lying Witness (Part 1)
lectures.description:
עֵד כְּזָבִים יֹאבֵד וְאִישׁ שׁוֹמֵעַ לָנֶצַח יְדַבֵּר:

This morning (3/30/22), in our Morning Mishlei shiur, we began working on a new pasuk. The first half is clearly about a witness who tells lies. The second half is decidedly less clear. We developed three approaches, then began working on the Metzudas David's approach. Tomorrow we'll refine that and learn the ideas from other meforshim (בג"ה).
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 21:27 - The Offering of the Rasha (Part 2)
lectures.description:
זֶבַח רְשָׁעִים תּוֹעֵבָה אַף כִּי בְזִמָּה יְבִיאֶנּוּ:

This morning (3/29/22), in our Morning Mishlei shiur, we continued working on yesterday's pasuk. Instead of developing the approaches we started yesterday, we devoted the full force of our minds to the commentary of the Metzudas David ... and we were rewarded for doing so! He answered all of our questions with his beautiful interpretation and ideas. We briefly explored two other approaches at the end, but didn't have time to develop them. Let me know if you come up with anything!
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 11:16 - In Pursuit of Kavod: Machiavellian vs. Mishleic
lectures.description:
אֵשֶׁת חֵן תִּתְמֹךְ כָּבוֹד וְעָרִיצִים יִתְמְכוּ עֹשֶׁר:

This evening (3/28/22), in our Monday Night Mishlei Shiur, we learned one of the most difficult pesukim in recent memory. The questions were powerful and it was difficult to pin down the subject matter of the pasuk. We worked really hard to develop a couple of approaches, but we were unsuccessful in "solving" the pasuk. We ended by learning Rabbeinu Yonah, who gave us a solid approach - albeit one which conveniently downplayed one of our major questions - and although we gained insight from his commentary (which is the basis of this title), we had to end shiur before we could fully develop his idea. If you manage to make it that far in the shiur and have any ideas, please let me know!
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 21:27 - The Offering of the Rasha (Part 1)
lectures.description:
זֶבַח רְשָׁעִים תּוֹעֵבָה אַף כִּי בְזִמָּה יְבִיאֶנּוּ:

This morning (3/28/22), in our Morning Mishlei shiur, we began a seemingly non-Mishleic pasuk about the korbanos of the wicked. We quickly found ourselves faced with a decision-tree of readings which led to different approaches to the pasuk. We didn't arrive at any conclusive interpretations today. Tomorrow we'll attempt to refine today's steps and to learn the meforshim (בג"ה).
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 21:25-26 - The Lethal Desire of the Lazy Person (Part 4)
lectures.description:
תַּאֲוַת עָצֵל תְּמִיתֶנּוּ כִּי מֵאֲנוּ יָדָיו לַעֲשׂוֹת:

This morning (3/24/22), in our Morning Mishlei shiur, we concluded our analysis of this week's pesukim. After reviewing the insight from yesterday, we sharpened our own approach and Rabbeinu Yonah's approach. We then spent the last portion of shiur going over practical strategies for overcoming laziness based on James Clear's "Atomic Habits" and BJ Fogg's "Tiny Habits."
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 21:25-26 - The Lethal Desire of the Lazy Person (Part 3)
lectures.description:
תַּאֲוַת עָצֵל תְּמִיתֶנּוּ כִּי מֵאֲנוּ יָדָיו לַעֲשׂוֹת:

This morning (3/23/22), in our Morning Mishlei shiur, we continued to develop the approach we took yesterday, inspired by Rabbeinu Yonah. We spent the first half of shiur developing a "horseshoe theory" about the developmental trajectories of the leitz and the atzel, and we spent the second half of shiur working on the second half of the last pasuk. Our goal tomorrow will be to complete our analysis AND identify some practical techniques for overcoming laziness (בג"ה).
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 21:25-26 - The Lethal Desire of the Lazy Person (Part 2)
lectures.description:
תַּאֲוַת עָצֵל תְּמִיתֶנּוּ כִּי מֵאֲנוּ יָדָיו לַעֲשׂוֹת:

This morning (3/22/22), in our Morning Mishlei shiur, we refined the idea we were developing yesterday about how the lazy person is in a constant state of suffering even in the realm of pleasure-seeking, as opposed to the tzadik who experiences the opposite. Rabbeinu Yonah gave us another step in the idea, but there's far more to explore here, and that is what we intend to do tomorrow (בג"ה).
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 11:15 - Who Should Hate Handshakes?
lectures.description:
רַע יֵרוֹעַ כִּי עָרַב זָר וְשֹׂנֵא תֹקְעִים בּוֹטֵחַ:

This evening (3/21/22), in our Monday Night Mishlei Shiur, we learned a pasuk which, at first glance, seemed to give anti-Mishleic (and anti-social) advice. Additionally, it was a challenge to figure out what this pasuk was even talking about. Thankfully, we developed several approaches which led to some very practical ideas with far-reaching implications, and we learned an additional insight from Rabbeinu Yonah.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 21:25-26 - The Lethal Desire of the Lazy Person (Part 1)
lectures.description:
תַּאֲוַת עָצֵל תְּמִיתֶנּוּ כִּי מֵאֲנוּ יָדָיו לַעֲשׂוֹת:

This morning (3/21/22), in our Morning Mishlei shiur, we began a Mishlei couplet on laziness. We raised a TON of questions and made some moves, but we'll have to wait until tomorrow to see how these play out with the help of the meforshim (בג"ה).
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 11:14 - A Strategy for Generating Strategies
lectures.description:
בְּאֵין תַּחְבֻּלוֹת יִפׇּל עָם וּתְשׁוּעָה בְּרֹב יוֹעֵץ:

This evening (3/14/22), in our Monday Night Mishlei Shiur, we learned a pasuk about the importance of strategies and abundant counsel. The challenge was understand the context and the lack of qualifications (e.g. Why "strategies" rather than "good strategies"? Why "abundant" counsel rather than "wise counsel"?) By putting our heads together in an effort to generate "abundant counsel," we came up with one nice approach together, and then explored some of the ideas in the meforshim.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei Bekius on Leitzim - Part 4 (Rabbeinu Yonah on Mishlei 14:6)
lectures.description: This morning (3/10/22), in our Morning Mishlei shiur, we wrapped up this round of "Mishlei Bekius on Leitzim" by examining the one quality we hadn't yet thought about: sichah bateilah ("idle chatter"). Thankfully, Rabbeinu Yonah explains this in his commentary on Mishlei 14:6, which is one of the pesukim that gave us the most trouble in our bekius overview.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei Bekius on Leitzim - Part 3
lectures.description: This morning (3/9/22), in our Morning Mishlei shiur, we concluded our survey of all the pesukim in Mishlei which mention leitz, along with our surface-level analysis and observations. We concluded by reading the first Rabbeinu Yonah on leitzim. Tomorrow the plan is to conclude this round of the sugya by learning Rabbeinu Yonah's commentary on select leitz-themed pesukim.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei Bekius on Leitzim - Part 2
lectures.description: This morning (3/8/22), in our Morning Mishlei shiur, we began with a methodology tip on how to learn the five megillos. Next, we reviewed all the pesukim we covered yesterday, reaping tremendous rewards in the process. After that, we learned five more pesukim, following our bekius approach and objective from yesterday. We hope to conclude our bekius overview tomorrow (בג"ה).
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 20:19 - On Gossip, Secrets, and Trust (Part 2)
lectures.description:
גּוֹלֶה סּוֹד הוֹלֵךְ רָכִיל וּלְפֹתֶה שְׂפָתָיו לֹא תִתְעָרָב:

Tonight (3/7/22), in our Monday Night Mishlei Shiur, we continued the topic from last week by learning a pasuk whose first half is the inverse of Mishlei 11:13. We began by approaching this pasuk afresh without going out of our way to tie it into the previous one, and we succeeded in coming up with several nice ideas. Afterwards, we learned the commentaries of Rabbeinu Yonah, Metzudas David, and Saadia Gaon.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei Bekius on Leitzim - Part 1
lectures.description: This morning (3/7/22), in our Morning Mishlei shiur, we deviated from our usual daily routine. Since we started developing a new approach to the Mishleic personality of the leitz (scorner) last week, we decided to take a couple of days to do a bekius (overview / covering-ground) survey of ALL the pesukim in Mishlei which mention this personality. Instead of analyzing these pesukim in-depth, we translated each pasuk and then made some initial observations about the characteristics emphasized in the pesukim. We got through half of the pesukim today and we plan on doing the other half tomorrow (בג"ה), at which point, we'll learn more of Rabbeinu Yonah's commentary on these pesukim.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 21:24 - The Leitz Reexamined (Part 2)
lectures.description:
זֵד יָהִיר לֵץ שְׁמוֹ עוֹשֶׂה בְּעֶבְרַת זָדוֹן:

This morning (3/3/22), in our Morning Mishlei shiur (which was only 30 minutes on account of Rosh Chodesh), we began by reviewing and refining what we said yesterday. Although this was worthwhile, it only left us with a few minutes to work on the chidush according to Rabbeinu Yonah. We developed an approach and formulated further questions raised by that approach, but we'll have to wait until next week (בג"ה) to revisit them.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 21:24 - The Leitz Reexamined (Part 1)
lectures.description:
זֵד יָהִיר לֵץ שְׁמוֹ עוֹשֶׂה בְּעֶבְרַת זָדוֹן:

This morning (3/2/22), in our Morning Mishlei shiur, we learned the pasuk which explicitly defines the Mishleic personality of the leitz (scoffer). I've learned and taught this pasuk dozens of times, and I was hoping for a new insight. Thankfully, that's exactly what we got, thanks to the thinking of two of our talmidim: one who interpreted yesterday's pasuk, and another who interpreted today's pasuk in light of that idea. This is already a contender for my favorite Mishlei shiur of the 2021-2022 year.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 21:23 - Guarding Your Mouth, Tongue, and Soul (Part 2)
lectures.description:
שֹׁמֵר פִּיו וּלְשׁוֹנוֹ שֹׁמֵר מִצָּרוֹת נַפְשׁוֹ:

This morning (3/1/22), in our Morning Mishlei shiur, we continued our analysis of yesterday's pasuk and found two Rishonim who helped us develop our approach: Rabbeinu Yonah and, surprisingly, the Rambam. We delved a bit into the Rambam's other statements about how we ought and ought not to speak, and then tied our understanding of the pasuk together at the end.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 26:9 - A Thorn in the Hand of a Drunkard (Part 2)
lectures.description:
חוֹחַ עָלָה בְיַד שִׁכּוֹר וּמָשָׁל בְּפִי כְסִילִים:

This morning (1/13/22), in our Morning Mishlei shiur, we learned the Meiri's commentary on this entire set of pesukim (26:6-9). He offered a number of different interpretations, some of which corresponded to what we had said in the past, and others of which were new. We ended off by starting to learn the Malbim's commentary on 26:9-10, but didn't have much time to get into 10.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 26:9 - A Thorn in the Hand of a Drunkard (Part 1)
lectures.description:
חוֹחַ עָלָה בְיַד שִׁכּוֹר וּמָשָׁל בְּפִי כְסִילִים:

This morning (1/12/22), in our Morning Mishlei shiur, we began our analysis of the third and final pasuk in our series on the topic of "how fools use Mishlei." We came up with three approaches of our own, the third of which roughly corresponded to that of Saadia Gaon and Ibn Kaspi. Tomorrow (בג"ה) we'll learn more meforshim on this pasuk - and the Meiri on all three.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 26:8 - The Dangers of Honoring a Ksil (Part 2)
lectures.description:
כִּצְרוֹר אֶבֶן בְּמַרְגֵּמָה כֵּן נוֹתֵן לִכְסִיל כָּבוֹד:

This morning (1/11/22), in our Morning Mishlei shiur, we continued our analysis of yesterday's pasuk. After recapping a related idea from last NIGHT's Mishlei pasuk (11:9), we recapped our approaches from yesterday and then learned two explanations: one from Metzudas David on our pasuk and the other from Rabbeinu Yonah on Avos 4:1. Both meforshim took our mashal in ways we hadn't even considered yesterday. Tomorrow (בג"ה) we'll begin the last pasuk in our "sidequest" sugya before taking a two week break.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 11:9 - How Tzadikim Evade Flattery
lectures.description:
בְּפֶה חָנֵף יַשְׁחִת רֵעֵהוּ וּבְדַעַת צַדִּיקִים יֵחָלֵצוּ:

This evening (1/10/22), in our Monday Night Mishlei Shiur, we learned yet another pasuk about tzadikim. This time, they were contrasted with someone other than the rasha. After experimenting with several different approaches and translations, we took up Rabbeinu Yonah's commentary, which led to some eye-opening insights about the dangers of flattery and how tzadikim use their unique knowledge to protect themselves.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 26:8 - The Dangers of Honoring a Ksil (Part 1)
lectures.description:
כִּצְרוֹר אֶבֶן בְּמַרְגֵּמָה כֵּן נוֹתֵן לִכְסִיל כָּבוֹד:

This morning (1/10/22), in our Morning Mishlei shiur, we began a new pasuk as a continuation of the sugya we started last week. This pasuk appears to be a simple analogy about giving honor to a ksil. The more we analyzed it, the more uncertain we were about the nuances of the analogy and the parameters of the idea. We ended up developing a few approaches, including an idea from Saadia Gaon who translates the pasuk in a completely different way. Tomorrow (בג"ה) the plan is to learn through a bunch of other meforshim.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 26:7 - A Mashal with a Limp (Part 2)
lectures.description:
דַּלְיוּ שֹׁקַיִם מִפִּסֵּחַ וּמָשָׁל בְּפִי כְסִילִים:

This morning (1/7/22), in our Morning Mishlei shiur, we continued our analysis of the pasuk we started on Monday. Today was quite the fruitful day! We came away with a good 6-10 ideas, depending on how you count. I'm looking forward to continuing next week (בג"ה) with the next two pesukim on the same theme.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 26:7 - A Mashal with a Limp (Part 1)
lectures.description:
דַּלְיוּ שֹׁקַיִם מִפִּסֵּחַ וּמָשָׁל בְּפִי כְסִילִים:

This morning (1/3/22), in our Morning Mishlei shiur, we took a detour to start a Mishlei sugya in 26:7-9. My interest in these pesukim was prompted by a quotation from Amos Tversky (Israeli cognitive and mathematical psychologist, and recipient of the MacArthur "genius grant"). Two (and possibly three) of these pesukim are about how a Mishleic fool relates to mashalim. I'd like to do these pesukim this week, and possibly into next week. Today we had a shorter session in which we developed two approaches to 26:7. Tomorrow we'll learn the meforshim (בג"ה).
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 21:16 - Resting in the Congregation of the Dead
lectures.description:
אָדָם תּוֹעֶה מִדֶּרֶךְ הַשְׂכֵּל בִּקְהַל רְפָאִים יָנוּחַ:

This morning (12/30/21), in our Morning Mishlei shiur, we began a new, dramatic pasuk. We came up with a really nice interpretation which was beautifully expanded upon by the Rav in Halakhic Man. We came up with what we THINK is a good understanding of the Ralbag, and read the Meiri as well. We may or may not continue this pasuk tomorrow, depending on who plans on coming to shiur.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 21:15 - Joy in Justice and its Opposite (Part 2)
lectures.description:
שִׂמְחָה לַצַּדִּיק עֲשׂוֹת מִשְׁפָּט וּמְחִתָּה לְפֹעֲלֵי אָוֶן:

This morning (12/29/21) we continued with the pasuk we learned yesterday. After developing an additional original approach, we learned another nice idea from the Meiri, then we went back to the Rabbeinu Yonah from yesterday, and we ended with Rashi's "classically Rashi" type of explanation which we didn't have time to flesh out.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 21:15 - Joy in Justice and its Opposite (Part 1)
lectures.description:
שִׂמְחָה לַצַּדִּיק עֲשׂוֹת מִשְׁפָּט וּמְחִתָּה לְפֹעֲלֵי אָוֶן:

This morning (12/28/21) we began a new syntactically ambiguous pasuk that has something to do with the joy experienced by the tzadik when justice is done. Beyond that, our pasuk can be read in a number of ways. Today we developed two (or two-and-a-half) explanations on our own and read two meforshim whose commentaries reflected those explanations - at least, in part. Tomorrow (בג"ה) we will learn other approaches in the other meforshim.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 11:8 - How the Rasha Gets Into the Trouble from Which the Tzadik Escaped
lectures.description:
צַדִּיק מִצָּרָה נֶחֱלָץ וַיָּבֹא רָשָׁע תַּחְתָּיו:

This evening (12/27/21), in our Monday Night Mishlei Shiur, we enjoyed had a "riddle style" pasuk that was quite straightforward to read. We managed to get several nice ideas from it which contributed to our continually evolving understanding of the Mishlei tzadik and the Mishleic rasha.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 21:14 - Secret Gifts, Bribes, and Anger (Part 3)
lectures.description:
מַתָּן בַּסֵּתֶר יִכְפֶּה אָף וְשֹׁחַד בַּחֵק חֵמָה עַזָּה:

This morning (12/22/21) we continued plumbing the depths of our pasuk. We began with some pshat interpretations from the Malbim and Radak, then analyzed the first of the Meiri's derech nistar explanations, and concluded by reading his second derech nistar explanation and a few midrashim which we didn't have time to analyze. This ended up being quite a rich pasuk (no pun intended)!
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 21:14 - Secret Gifts, Bribes, and Anger (Part 2)
lectures.description:
מַתָּן בַּסֵּתֶר יִכְפֶּה אָף וְשֹׁחַד בַּחֵק חֵמָה עַזָּה:

This morning (12/21/21) we continued learning yesterday's pasuk. After refining the approach we took yesterday, we learned the commentaries of the Meiri and Rabbeinu Yonah, who connect this pasuk to the previous one, which is about giving tzedakah. We plan on spending at least one more day on this pasuk, and then learning through some of the practical halachos of tzedakah which pertain to both pesukim.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 11:7 - The Hopeless Death of the Rasha
lectures.description:
בְּמוֹת אָדָם רָשָׁע תֹּאבַד תִּקְוָה וְתוֹחֶלֶת אוֹנִים אָבָדָה:

This evening (12/20/21), in our Monday Night Mishlei Shiur, we enjoyed a respite from the "teeth-breaking" pesukim about the tam and the yashar with a nice pasuk about the death of a rasha! The reading, translation, and questions were fairly straight-forward, and we had success in working out two approaches and bringing them to fruition with the help of the meforshim. Both ideas are practical in very different ways.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 21:14 - Secret Gifts, Bribes, and Anger (Part 1)
lectures.description:
מַתָּן בַּסֵּתֶר יִכְפֶּה אָף וְשֹׁחַד בַּחֵק חֵמָה עַזָּה:

This morning (12/20/21) we began a new pasuk. Like most pesukim which LOOK simple, this one turned out to be difficult, even to read and translate. The problem we encountered was the pasuk's generality, which leant it to many possible readings. We weren't even sure if the pasuk was endorsing this behavior, warning against it, or remaining neutral! We read the Metzudas David's commentary in the last minute of shiur, but I have a feeling we'll see a variety of approaches when we learn through the other meforshim tomorrow (בג"ה).
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 21:13 - The Consequences of Shutting Your Ear to the Poor (Part 2)
lectures.description:
אֹטֵם אׇזְנוֹ מִזַּעֲקַת דָּל גַּם הוּא יִקְרָא וְלֹא יֵעָנֶה:

This morning (12/16/21) we continued our analysis of yesterday's pasuk. Thanks to the Malbim's definition of "dal" - we were able to develop and expand upon the approaches we came up with yesterday. We also saw new ideas in the commentaries of Rabbeinu Yonah and the Meiri.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 21:12 - How the Tzadik Helps the Rasha Succeed (Part 2)
lectures.description:
אֹטֵם אׇזְנוֹ מִזַּעֲקַת דָּל גַּם הוּא יִקְרָא וְלֹא יֵעָנֶה:

This morning (12/15/21) we began a new and "spicy" pasuk which states a very clear midah kneged midah consequence. We developed two approaches and nodded our heads to a third, which we didn't have time to explore. Tomorrow we'll consult the meforshim (בג"ה).
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 21:12 - How the Tzadik Helps the Rasha Succeed (Part 2)
lectures.description:
מַשְׂכִּיל צַדִּיק לְבֵית רָשָׁע מְסַלֵּף רְשָׁעִים לָרָע:

This morning (12/14/21) we began with a brief discussion about giving tzedakah on Asarah b'Teves (unrelated to our pasuk in Mishlei), we reviewed what we said yesterday and developed a variant on my own approach to the pasuk, and then learned four excellent interpretations of our pasuk: that of the Metzudas David, Rabbeinu Yonah, Shadal, and Meiri's derech nistar.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 11:6 - How Loyalty to Reality Pays Off
lectures.description:
צִדְקַת יְשָׁרִים תַּצִּילֵם וּבְהַוַּת בֹּגְדִים יִלָּכֵדוּ:

This evening (12/13/21), in our Monday Night Mishlei Shiur, we learned yet ANOTHER extremely difficult pasuk on the subject of the yashar (upright) and the bogeid (Mishleic traitor) - one which looked almost identical to the previous pasuk, and was even identified as such by the Radak! After some initial theorizing with approaches that had potential, we learned the Rabbeinu Yonah's commentary, who offered a beautiful insight into one of the core benefits of learning Mishlei.

If you're not in the mood to break your teeth, it might be a good idea to start the shiur, and once we raise all the questions, skip to about an hour in, when we start the Rabbeinu Yonah.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 21:12 - How the Tzadik Helps the Rasha Succeed (Part 1)
lectures.description:
מַשְׂכִּיל צַדִּיק לְבֵית רָשָׁע מְסַלֵּף רְשָׁעִים לָרָע:

This morning (12/13/21) we began learning a pasuk which presents itself as counterintuitive no matter how you read it. We played around with a couple of approaches and ended with my favorite explanation, which I first heard from my brother. Tomorrow we'll consult the meforshim (בג"ה).
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 21:11 - How the Pesi Learns from Others (Part 3)
lectures.description:
בַּעֲנׇשׁ לֵץ יֶחְכַּם פֶּתִי וּבְהַשְׂכִּיל לְחָכָם יִקַּח דָּעַת:

This morning (12/9/21) we spent a third day on our pasuk. We began with some additional points on two of yesterday's approaches. We then learned the Meiri's derech nistar approach, which we supplemented with a nice idea from Drashos ha'Ran. We then looked through a flurry of other meforshim, who gave us additional nuances to our understanding.

Note: around 42 minutes into the shiur, one of the guys reads something from Urban Dictionary which uses the word "arse," which he read aloud several times not knowing that it is British profanity. I edited it out of the YouTube video, but (frankly) I don't have time to edit it out of the audio. Just know that he didn't mean anything by it.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 21:11 - How the Pesi Learns from Others (Part 2)
lectures.description:
בַּעֲנׇשׁ לֵץ יֶחְכַּם פֶּתִי וּבְהַשְׂכִּיל לְחָכָם יִקַּח דָּעַת:

This morning (12/8/21) we continued learning yesterday's pasuk about how the pesi learns. After refining yesterday's approach, we learned the derech nigleh explanation given by the Meiri, followed by Rabbeinu Yonah, which also led us to his commentary on the very similar 19:25. We intend to spend one more day on this pasuk.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 21:11 - How the Pesi Learns from Others (Part 1)
lectures.description:
בַּעֲנׇשׁ לֵץ יֶחְכַּם פֶּתִי וּבְהַשְׂכִּיל לְחָכָם יִקַּח דָּעַת:

This morning (12/7/21) we began a new pasuk, which is certainly about the pesi (naive simpleton), but might also be about the chacham (wise person), and maybe even the leitz (scoffer). Today we developed an approach on the assumption that the pasuk is about the pesi and how he learns from the punishment of the leitz and the behavior of the chacham. Tomorrow we plan on exploring other approaches.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 21:10 - The Illusory Favor of the Rasha (Part 1)
lectures.description:
נֶפֶשׁ רָשָׁע אִוְּתָה רָע, לֹא יֻחַן בְּעֵינָיו רֵעֵהוּ:

This morning (12/1/21) we began a new pasuk - the first half of which seemed obvious, and the second half of which seemed like a non-sequitur. After exploring several approaches today, we arrived at a nice explanation, based in part on Rabbeinu Yonah. Tomorrow we plan on checking out what the other meforshim have to say.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 21:9 - Precarious Solitude vs. Good Friends and a Toxic Wife (Part 2)
lectures.description:
טוֹב לָשֶׁבֶת עַל פִּנַּת גָּג מֵאֵשֶׁת מִדְיָנִים וּבֵית חָבֶר:

This morning (11/30/21) we continued our analysis of yesterday's pasuk, beginning with a shockingly different translation in which "beis chaver" is translated not as "a house of a friend" but "a house of witchcraft." If you're interested in an explanation of our pasuk which connects ancient witchcraft with modern social media, or in the Meiri's allegorical interpretation of "dwelling on the corner of a roof" as "relying on tradition without rational proof," then you'll be in for a treat with this shiur!
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 11:5 - The Progress and Pitfall of the Tamim
lectures.description:
צִדְקַת תָּמִים תְּיַשֵּׁר דַּרְכּוֹ, וּבְרִשְׁעָתוֹ יִפֹּל רָשָׁע:

"Breaking your teeth on Gemara" is a well-known idiom. This evening (11/29/21), in our Monday Night Mishlei Shiur, we "broke our teeth on Mishlei." The the pasuk we learned wasn't inherently difficult. Some meforshim explicitly said that there are no new ideas here. We came up with three nice explanations. The "teeth-breaking" took place in the discussion and anaylsis, which required fluency in a number of nuanced Mishleic concepts, and the difficulty level kicked into high gear once we attempted to learn Rabbeinu Yonah's commentary. If you're going to listen to this shiur, know that it's not for the faint of heart.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 21:9 - Precarious Solitude vs. Good Friends and a Toxic Wife (Part 1)
lectures.description:
טוֹב לָשֶׁבֶת עַל פִּנַּת גָּג מֵאֵשֶׁת מִדְיָנִים וּבֵית חָבֶר:

This morning (11/29/21) we began learning a pasuk about the deleterious effects of a "contentious wife." According to the approach we took today, based on the Malbim's commentary, it was clear that this is referring to the type of personality that we would characterize today as "toxic." We intend to explore other interpretations tomorrow.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 21:8 - Estranged by Your Own Inconsistency (Part 2)
lectures.description:
הֲפַכְפַּךְ דֶּרֶךְ אִישׁ וָזָר, וְזַךְ יָשָׁר פׇּעֳלוֹ:

This morning (11/23/21) we continued our analysis of yesterday's pasuk. We ended up with a handful of fruitful approaches - all of which yielded insight into decision-making, and none of which were completely refined. But such is the way of Mishlei: sometimes we gain more from the discussion itself than the final results.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 11:4 - Tzedakah Saves from Death Yet Again
lectures.description:
לֹא יוֹעִיל הוֹן בְּיוֹם עֶבְרָה וּצְדָקָה תַּצִּיל מִמָּוֶת:

This evening (11/22/21), in our Monday Night Mishlei Shiur, we learned a pasuk in chapter 11 which was nearly identical with a pasuk we learned over a year ago in chapter 10. The challenge was to see it in a new light and not just end up with a Mishleic cliche. Thanks to the Malbim, we succeeded!
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 21:8 - Estranged by Your Own Inconsistency (Part 1)
lectures.description:
הֲפַכְפַּךְ דֶּרֶךְ אִישׁ וָזָר, וְזַךְ יָשָׁר פׇּעֳלוֹ:

This morning (11/22/21) we began learning a pasuk with a highly dubious hapax legomenon and highly confusing wording. This led us down a little rabbit hole about what to do with such cases. For some reason, today's shiur ended up being way more chock-full of methodology - including a story about a group of ethnobotanists and a crab that I heard from Tim Ferriss and have been waiting for a legitimate excuse to deploy. We got some approaches brewing, and plan to return to the pasuk tomorrow, beginning with Saadia Gaon's commentary.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei Commentary Tier-Ranking
lectures.description: This morning (11/18/21) we had a special Mishlei Methodology shiur in which I ranked all the Mishlei commentaries I know of - not in terms of how OBJECTIVELY good they are, but in terms of how valuable I have PERSONALLY found them to be in my OWN twenty years of intensive Mishlei learning and teaching. After explaining the tiers in my ranking system, I go through each of the commentaries, comment on their styles and methods, discuss their pros and cons, and explain why I ranked them as I did. My hope is that this shiur will help those who want to learn Mishlei on their own but don't know which commentaries to use.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 21:7 - Fear-Inducing Plunder (Part 2)
lectures.description:
שֹׁד רְשָׁעִים יְגוֹרֵם כִּי מֵאֲנוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת מִשְׁפָּט:

This morning (11/17/21) we continued working on yesterday's pasuk. Since we had three times as many guys in shiur, we decided to analyze the pasuk from scratch. After exploring several approaches from the guys, we learned Saadia Gaon's commentary.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 21:7 - Fear-Inducing Plunder (Part 1)
lectures.description:
שֹׁד רְשָׁעִים יְגוֹרֵם כִּי מֵאֲנוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת מִשְׁפָּט:

This morning (11/16/21) we began learning a strange pasuk. This is one of those pesukim with "mix-and-match" translations, but no matter which way you slice it, the hava amina is weird. We came up with two approaches and some partial ideas, but we plan on revisiting it tomorrow with some more meforshim. We also suspect that some might tie it back to yesterday's pasuk.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 21:6 - Bank Accounts that Beat You to Death Before Vanishing
lectures.description:
פֹּעַל אֹצָרוֹת בִּלְשׁוֹן שָׁקֶר הֶבֶל נִדָּף מְבַקְשֵׁי מָוֶת:

This morning (11/15/21) we learned a pasuk which initially appeared to be too confusing to make ANY moves, but ended up feeling so "Mishleically cliche" that we had a hard time seeing a chidush. We ended up getting some nice insights, but not that earth-shattering chidush we were looking for - unless you count the Ralbag's highly "Gersonidean" explanation which we briefly touched upon at the end. We're planning to move on to the next pasuk tomorrow unless anyone has any "eureka" insights in the interim.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 11:3 - Rabbeinu Yonah on Tam, Yashar, and Bogeid
lectures.description:
תֻּמַּת יְשָׁרִים תַּנְחֵם וְסֶלֶף בֹּגְדִים יְשָׁדֵּם:

This evening (11/15/21), in our Monday Night Mishlei Shiur, we learned Rabbeinu Yonah's commentary on last week's pasuk. Rabbeinu Yonah begins with an exposition on the personalities of the tam and the yashar and then proceeds to explain our pasuk on that basis. I'll be honest: I was NOT optimistic about how tonight's shiur would turn out. Thankfully, the Monday Night Mishlei Crew pulled through. Not only were we able to understand (most of) Rabbeinu Yonah's ideas, but we were also able to grasp his nuanced approach to our pasuk. Even though this was a very different kind of shiur than our usual Monday Night Mishlei, it proved to be a triumphant evening in the world of ideas.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 21:5 - The Yields of Diligence and Haste (Part 2)
lectures.description:
מַחְשְׁבוֹת חָרוּץ אַךְ לְמוֹתָר וְכׇל אָץ אַךְ לְמַחְסוֹר:

This morning (11/11/21) we set out to learn the meforshim (plural) on yesterday's pasuk, but Rabbeinu Yonah's commentary was so rich that we spent the entire time delving into that! This was a very "meta-Mishlei" shiur in that we not only focused on decision-making, but we also discussed how to make decisions ABOUT decision-making. Rabbeinu Yonah's commentary tends to be great, but his interpretation of this pasuk was ::: chef's kiss ::: fantastic!
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 21:5 - The Yields of Diligence and Haste (Part 1)
lectures.description:
מַחְשְׁבוֹת חָרוּץ אַךְ לְמוֹתָר וְכׇל אָץ אַךְ לְמַחְסוֹר:

This morning (11/10/21) we began a pasuk with a clear topic: diligence versus haste. The implications of the pasuk were less clear: is diligence being depicted in a good light here, as we would expect from Mishlei, or is this pointing out a diligence-related flaw? We came up with a handful of approaches. Tomorrow we'll see what the meforshim say.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 21:4 - Furrows of the Wicked (Part 2)
lectures.description:
רוּם עֵינַיִם וּרְחַב לֵב נִר רְשָׁעִים חַטָּאת:

This morning (11/9/21) we continued our analysis of yesterday's pasuk, beginning with a review of yesterday's idea. We then attempted to support that approach with two meforshim (Radak and Rabbeinu Yonah), only to realize that they were saying something different. We then found a support (Ri Nachmias) for another reading of the pasuk we tried yesterday which ended up leading to a nice idea. We ended with two other readings of the pasuk: one which took it in a completely different direction, (Ralbag) and another which was a hybrid of previous ideas (Malbim).
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 11:3 - The Integrity of the Upright
lectures.description:
תֻּמַּת יְשָׁרִים תַּנְחֵם וְסֶלֶף בֹּגְדִים יְשָׁדֵּם:

This evening (11/8/21), in our Monday Night Mishlei Shiur, we tackled a VERY difficult pasuk in which literally every word needed to be defined conceptually. Not only that, but this pasuk introduced us to not one, not two, but THREE new Mishleic personality types: the tam, the yashar, and the bogeid. The beginning of our analysis was all over the place, but with a combination of teamwork and clear thinking, we were able to emerge with an awesome idea.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 21:4 - Furrows of the Wicked (Part 1)
lectures.description:
רוּם עֵינַיִם וּרְחַב לֵב נִר רְשָׁעִים חַטָּאת:

This morning (11/8/21) we started a pasuk which was doubly difficult to read, due to its idiomatic terminology and its ambiguous syntax. We struggled to work out viable approaches for most of the shiur and finally hit upon a good one in the last couple of minutes. Tomorrow we'll consult the meforshim.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 21:3 - Tzedakah and Mishpat vs. Sacrifice (Part 2)
lectures.description:
עֲשֹׂה צְדָקָה וּמִשְׁפָּט נִבְחָר לַי״י מִזָּבַח:

This morning (11/4/21) we continued our analysis of yesterday's pasuk by learning through six or seven meforshim. We were able to extract full ideas from some of them and partial ideas from others, but either way, we emerged with a clearer understanding of the relationship between korbanos and perfection than we had yesterday.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 21:3 - Tzedakah and Mishpat vs. Sacrifice (Part 1)
lectures.description:
עֲשֹׂה צְדָקָה וּמִשְׁפָּט נִבְחָר לַי״י מִזָּבַח:

This morning (11/3/21) we started learning a very non-Mishleic pasuk - "non-Mishleic" in the sense that it discusses korbanos. We developed three nice approaches on our own. Tomorrow the plan is to learn the meforshim, starting with Saadia Gaon, who connects this pasuk with the previous one.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 11:2 - Mishleic Tznius
lectures.description:
בָּא זָדוֹן וַיָּבֹא קָלוֹן וְאֶת צְנוּעִים חׇכְמָה:

This evening (11/1/21), in our Monday Night Mishlei Shiur, we learned Mishlei's take on tznius (modesty) and its relationship with chochmah. The pasuk was difficult in that it was quite vague - yet, we were able to come up with a good four or five solid ideas. I don't think it's an exaggeration to say that Mishlei's concept of tznius might evolve your view of tznius in general. But you can be the judge of that.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 21:2 - Subjective Evaluations vs. Hashem
lectures.description:
כׇּל דֶּרֶךְ אִישׁ יָשָׁר בְּעֵינָיו וְתֹכֵן לִבּוֹת י״י:

This morning (11/1/21) we learned one of those "Duh!" pesukim, which seem like they're stating an obvious idea. In cases like these, the challenge is to find an intellectual chidush (new insight), an emotional chidush, or both. We came up with three (or four) nice approaches which achieved these objectives, and we will most likely move on to the next pasuk next time.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 21:1 - Do Kings Have Free Will? (Part 1) (last 10 minutes of shiur)
lectures.description:
(NOTE: The internet went out 30 minutes in, which forced me to split the recording into Part A and Part B. If I had the time and the skill I'd merge the two videos into one, but at the present, I have neither.)

Mishlei 21:1 (Part B) Do Kings Have Free Will? (Part 1)

פַּלְגֵי מַיִם לֶב מֶלֶךְ בְּיַד י״י עַל כׇּל אֲשֶׁר יַחְפֹּץ יַטֶּנּוּ:

This morning (10/27/21) we began a new chapter with a zinger of a pasuk. The pasuk implies that Hashem controls the hearts of kings, which would appear to undermine the foundational principle of bechirah (free will). Today we attempted to understand the pasuk on our own. Tomorrow we will endeavor to learn the meforshim.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 21:1 - Do Kings Have Free Will? (Part 1) (first 35 minutes of shiur)
lectures.description:
(NOTE: The internet went out 30 minutes in, which forced me to split the recording into Part A and Part B. If I had the time and the skill I'd merge the two videos into one, but at the present, I have neither.)

Mishlei 21:1 (Part A) Do Kings Have Free Will? (Part 1)

פַּלְגֵי מַיִם לֶב מֶלֶךְ בְּיַד י״י עַל כׇּל אֲשֶׁר יַחְפֹּץ יַטֶּנּוּ:

This morning (10/27/21) we began a new chapter with a zinger of a pasuk. The pasuk implies that Hashem controls the hearts of kings, which would appear to undermine the foundational principle of bechirah (free will). Today we attempted to understand the pasuk on our own. Tomorrow we will endeavor to learn the meforshim.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 20:30 - Wounds that Purge and Polish Evil (Part 2)
lectures.description:
חַבֻּרוֹת פֶּצַע [תַּמְרוּק] (תמריק) בְּרָע וּמַכּוֹת חַדְרֵי בָטֶן:

This morning (10/26/21) we continued our learning of yesterday's pasuk. We began by reviewing the ideas we went over yesterday, including Rabbeinu Yonah's, for which we developed an approach. We then learned the Ralbag's creative interpretation, which led to some nice insights. We concluded with the Meiri and Ibn Kaspi, but didn't have sufficient time to fully develop their approaches.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 11:1 - Hashem Hates Deceitful Scales
lectures.description:
מֹאזְנֵי מִרְמָה תּוֹעֲבַת י״י וְאֶבֶן שְׁלֵמָה רְצוֹנוֹ:

This evening (10/25/21), in our Monday Night Mishlei Shiur, we learned a pasuk which came preloaded with a unique set of challenges. Not only is this pasuk a repition of what the Torah already says, but Shlomo HIMSELF essentially repeats this pasuk twice more in Sefer Mishlei (20:10 and 20:23). It was a challenge for me to approach this with fresh eyes, after having given shiurim on both those pesukim AND on the Torah's use of the term toeivah last year, so I had to count on the people in the shiur to find the ideas. Thankfully, they did! We got four interpretations of the pasuk from the participants along with two from the meforshim.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 20:30 - Wounds that Purge and Polish Evil (Part 1)
lectures.description:
חַבֻּרוֹת פֶּצַע [תַּמְרוּק] (תמריק) בְּרָע וּמַכּוֹת חַדְרֵי בָטֶן:

This morning (10/25/21) we began learning the final pasuk in Chapter 20. The translation proved to be difficult on account of the contronym "tamrook b'ra," which can either mean "to purge evil" (i.e. to get rid of it) or "to polish evil" (i.e. to accentuate it). We came up with three of our own approaches before turning to Rabbeinu Yonah (with a nod to Metzudas David). Tomorrow we'll go back and refine our understanding of their approaches, then see what the other meforshim have to say.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 20:29 - The Glory of Youths and Elders (Part 2)
lectures.description:
תִּפְאֶרֶת בַּחוּרִים כֹּחָם וַהֲדַר זְקֵנִים שֵׂיבָה:

This morning (10/21/21), after reviewing what we covered yesterday, we learned several meforshim - each of which led to new and beneficial insights. Considering how relatively "bland" this pasuk appeared at first blush, we were pleasantly surprised about how rich it ended up being.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 20:29 - The Glory of Youths and Elders (Part 1)
lectures.description:
תִּפְאֶרֶת בַּחוּרִים כֹּחָם וַהֲדַר זְקֵנִים שֵׂיבָה:

This morning (10/20/21) we began a new pasuk which seemed to focus on "non-Mishleic" qualities, without any Mishleic implications. We developed several nice explanations, supported by meforshim on non-Mishlei sources. Tomorrow we'll see what the meforshim on Mishlei have to say.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 20:28 - The Role of Chesed and Emes in the Monarchy (Part 2)
lectures.description:
חֶסֶד וֶאֱמֶת יִצְּרוּ מֶלֶךְ וְסָעַד בַּחֶסֶד כִּסְאוֹ:

This morning (10/19/21) we continued our analysis of yesterday's pasuk about the role of chesed and emes) in relation to the king and his subjects. After reviewing yesterday's approach and hearing a new one, we turned to the meforshim. We arrived at three approaches: (1) Metzudas David, Shadal, and Rabbeinu Yonah, (2) Meiri's "derech nigleh" approach to Mishlei 20:27-28, and (3) Meiri's "derech nistar" approach to Mishlei 20:28, which led us to review the Rambam's "middle path" approach, along with the parable of the farmer and the parable of Nachum Ish Gamzu.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 20:28 - The Role of Chesed and Emes in the Monarchy (Part 1)
lectures.description:
חֶסֶד וֶאֱמֶת יִצְּרוּ מֶלֶךְ וְסָעַד בַּחֶסֶד כִּסְאוֹ:

This morning (10/18/21) we started learning a pasuk about the role of chesed and emes (whatever those mean) in relation to the king and his subjects. We spent today working out a straightforward approach which accounted for the asymmetry in the structure of the pasuk, and the counterintuitiveness of the passive and active parties. Tomorrow we'll consult the meforshim.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 10:31-32: How to Speak (and Lie) Like a Tzadik
lectures.description:
(לא) פִּי צַדִּיק יָנוּב חׇכְמָה וּלְשׁוֹן תַּהְפֻּכוֹת תִּכָּרֵת:
(לב) שִׂפְתֵי צַדִּיק יֵדְעוּן רָצוֹן וּפִי רְשָׁעִים תַּהְפֻּכוֹת:

This evening (10/18/21), in our Monday Night Mishlei Shiur, we learned the last two pesukim of Chapter 10, which most meforshim treat as one long pasuk. This time our own analysis led us directly to the Rabbeinu Yonah's extensive commentary, which left us with a beautiful idea about how the essential difference between a Mishleic tzadik and a rasha is epitomized in their speech. It was a fitting way to conclude Chapter 10, which we began 365 days ago.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 20:27 - Man's Soul is Hashem's Lamp (Part 2)
lectures.description:
נֵר י״י נִשְׁמַת אָדָם חֹפֵשׂ כׇּל חַדְרֵי בָטֶן:

This morning (10/14/21) we continued our analysis of yesterday's pasuk, beginning with a review of what we said. We then attempted to understand the pasuk according to the second - and more difficult - reading, according to which Hashem "uses" the soul of man as a lamp to search out the chambers of the belly. We encountered several approaches and gleaned some insights, but ultimately agreed that what we said yesterday was a more satisfying explanation.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 20:27 - Man's Soul is Hashem's Lamp (Part 1)
lectures.description:
נֵר י״י נִשְׁמַת אָדָם חֹפֵשׂ כׇּל חַדְרֵי בָטֶן:

This morning (10/13/21) we began a new pasuk which, at first glance, seems very non-Mishleic. It appears to be a factual statement about man's soul and it's relationship to God's knowledge. We developed a solid idea based on one reading of the pasuk. Tomorrow we'll see what the meforshim say about that approach, and what they say about the route we didn't take.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 20:26 - Winnowing the Wicked (Part 2)
lectures.description:
מְזָרֶה רְשָׁעִים מֶלֶךְ חָכָם וַיָּשֶׁב עֲלֵיהֶם אוֹפָן:

This morning (10/12/21) we continued our analysis of yesterday's pasuk - this time, with the help of the meforshim. Shadal and Malbim both learn the pasuk to be about the samem topic: how a wise judge gets the wicked to confess (although Shadal, in our view, provides a more compelling reading of the words in the pasuk). We spent today unpacking and refining our understanding of their ideas. Tomorrow the plan is to move on to the next pasuk.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 10:30 - Do Tzadikim Falter?
lectures.description:
צַדִּיק לְעוֹלָם בַּל יִמּוֹט וּרְשָׁעִים לֹא יִשְׁכְּנוּ אָרֶץ:

This evening (10/11/21), in our Monday Night Mishlei Shiur, we learned yet another difficult pasuk. This one was fairly easy to read, but proved difficult to get a unified chidush (novel insight) from, even with our abundance of ideas about tzadikim and reshaim from earlier in the perek. We certainly gave it our effort and arrived at some nice insights, but there definitely remains more to be done.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 20:26 - Winnowing the Wicked (Part 1)
lectures.description:
מְזָרֶה רְשָׁעִים מֶלֶךְ חָכָם וַיָּשֶׁב עֲלֵיהֶם אוֹפָן:

This morning (10/11/21) we began a new pasuk about how a wise king ought to deal with the wicked. There are a couple of ambiguitiies in the translation which suggest a number of different directions. We spent this morning trying to figure out the first half of the pasuk, but didn't make much progress on the second half. The plan for tomorrow is to turn to the meforshim for assistance.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 20:25 - A Confusing Pasuk About Particular Snares (Part 3)
lectures.description:
מוֹקֵשׁ אָדָם יָלַע קֹדֶשׁ, וְאַחַר נְדָרִים לְבַקֵּר:

This morning (10/8/21) was our third day on this pasuk. After reviewing yesterday's idea from the Meiri, we learned three more interpretations: two from the Meiri and one from Rabbeinu Yonah, who tied this into Monday's pasuk (10/4). It may have taken us three days, but we ultimately got some nice insights from this pasuk!
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 20:25 - A Confusing Pasuk About Particular Snares (Part 2)
lectures.description:
מוֹקֵשׁ אָדָם יָלַע קֹדֶשׁ, וְאַחַר נְדָרִים לְבַקֵּר:

Yesterday we had one goal: be to learn at least ONE idea from this very confusing pasuk. This morning (10/7/21) we succeeded, thanks to the Meiri and the Rambam! Since the Meiri gives several other interpretations which we didn't have time for, we plan on continuing in the Meiri tomorrow.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 20:25 - A Confusing Pasuk About Particular Snares (Part 1)
lectures.description:
מוֹקֵשׁ אָדָם יָלַע קֹדֶשׁ, וְאַחַר נְדָרִים לְבַקֵּר:

This morning (10/6/21) we began a pasuk which proved to be EXTREMELY difficult to translate. Every translation and commentary we consulted seemed to read the pasuk differently. We spent most of our (shorter) shiur today trying to arrive at a coherent translation, and we spent the last few minutes trying to make sense of Saadia Gaon's and Metzudas David's explanations ... but to no avail. Tomorrow our goal will be to learn at least ONE idea from this pasuk!
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 20:24 - Man's Steps and the Limits of Human Understanding (Part 2)
lectures.description:
מֵי״י מִצְעֲדֵי גָבֶר וְאָדָם מַה יָּבִין דַּרְכּוֹ:

This morning (10/5/21) we began by reviewing our four approaches from yesterday. We then consulted the meforshim - some of whom took similar approaches to ours, and some of whom added new points. We concluded by tying the ideas we learned to the berachah we say every morning.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 10:29 - Derech Hashem as Rampart and Ruin
lectures.description:
מָעוֹז לַתֹּם דֶּרֶךְ י״י וּמְחִתָּה לְפֹעֲלֵי אָוֶן:

This evening (10/4/21), in our Monday Night Mishlei Shiur, we learned a pasuk that was difficult to translate and even more difficult to understand. We developed several related approaches and did our best to hone them, thanks to Rabbeinu Yonah, and although we didn't QUITE reach the level of clarity that I prefer, we at least managed to uncover some nice ideas. We read through a few additional commentaries at the end, just to get a glimpse of alternative approaches.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 20:24 - Man's Steps and the Limits of Human Understanding (Part 1)
lectures.description:
מֵי״י מִצְעֲדֵי גָבֶר וְאָדָם מַה יָּבִין דַּרְכּוֹ:

This morning (10/4/21) we began learning the pasuk which, according to some, is the source-pasuk for the berachah of "ha'meichin mitzadei gaver." We spent this morning's learning session attempting to develop our own approaches. Tomorrow we'll consult the meforshim.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 20:23 - Another Pasuk About Deceitful Weights and Measures?!
lectures.description:
תּוֹעֲבַת י״י אֶבֶן וָאָבֶן וּמֹאזְנֵי מִרְמָה לֹא טוֹב:

This morning (9/17/21) we encountered yet ANOTHER pasuk about deceitful weights and measures! We had enough difficulty with the pasuk earlier in the perek, which seemed to be a repetition of what is already stated in the Torah. What does this NEW seemingly redundant pasuk come to add? Thankfully, Saadia Gaon's translation and commentary held the key to a new idea.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 20:22 - Hope to Hashem, the Avenger (Part 2)
lectures.description:
אַל תֹּאמַר אֲשַׁלְּמָה רָע קַוֵּה לַי״י וְיֹשַׁע לָךְ:

This morning (9/14/21) we continued our analysis of yesterday's pasuk. We clarified our understanding of MOST of Rabbeinu Yonah's approach, but didn't succeed in figuring out the last part. Thankfully, Radak, Ralbag, R' Moshe Alsheikh came to the rescue and provided us with their own insightful approaches. We concluded with a point about what we should and shouldn't be doing when we ask Hashem to destroy our enemies.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 10:28 - How Not to Have Your Hopes Dashed AND Be Perpetually Happy
lectures.description:
תּוֹחֶלֶת צַדִּיקִים שִׂמְחָה וְתִקְוַת רְשָׁעִים תֹּאבֵד:

This evening (9/13/21), in our first Monday Night Mishlei Shiur of the 2021-2022 year, we learned a pasuk which proved difficult to read at first. Our analysis led us to an idea that was expanded upon by the Rabbeinu Yonah. If the promise in the title of the shiur sounds too good to be true, then chances are that you're operating in the framework of the rasha, which means that this pasuk is for you!
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 20:22 - Hope to Hashem, the Avenger (Part 1)
lectures.description:
אַל תֹּאמַר אֲשַׁלְּמָה רָע קַוֵּה לַי״י וְיֹשַׁע לָךְ:

This morning (9/13/21) we began our analysis of a seemingly non-Mishleic pasuk. The questions were straightforward, and we took a few steps on our own before turning to the meforshim. The meforshim did a thorough job explaining the case in the first half of the pasuk, but shed very little light on the mechanics of the second half, which is what we'll attempt to decipher tomorrow.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 28:13 - How to Obtain Mercy for Wrongdoing from People and God
lectures.description:
מְכַסֶּה פְשָׁעָיו לֹא יַצְלִיחַ וּמוֹדֶה וְעֹזֵב יְרֻחָם:

This morning (9/10/21), in our inaugural morning Mishlei shiur of 2021-2022, we learned a pasuk that is very relevant to the Aseres Ymei Teshuvah. First we learned the pasuk according to the most basic pshat, namely, that it's about how to maximize the chance that you will be forgiven when you wrong a fellow human being. Then we learned the pasuk in reference to obtaining mercy from Hashem. We concluded with a theory about how this is the basis of the entire vidui of Yom ha'Kippurim.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: 8th Yahrtzeit for Shani Feder - Parenting with Mishlei
lectures.speaker: Rabbi E. Feder

lectures.title: Torah vs. Heresy #21: Lady Folly's Last Stand - Mishlei 9:13-18
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Aron Zimmer

lectures.title: Mishlei 19:23 - Yiras Hashem: the Keto Diet of the Soul
lectures.description: This morning (3/17/21 at YBT), armed with our definition of yiras Hashem from yesterday's pesukim (1:7 and 15:33), we continued our analysis of Mishlei 19:23 and arrived at a nice idea which happened to coincide with some Stoic ideas that I've been discussing on The Stoic Jew Podcast lately (shameless plug: https://thestoicjew.buzzsprout.com). "How," you may ask, "is yiras Hashem comparable to Keto?" I guess you'll have to listen to find out!
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 1:7 and 15:33 - On Yiras Hashem (Fear of God)
lectures.description: This morning (3/16/21 at YBT) we began our analysis of Mishlei 19:23, the next pasuk in our perek, but because this was the first pasuk we've learned this year which mentioned yiras Hashem (fear of God), we decided to take a detour to the two main pesukim in Mishlei on that topic. Although our interpretation of those two pesukim still need a bit of work, we emerged with a clear enough definition of yiras Hashem to be able to tackle 19:23 tomorrow.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 10:19 - The Trouble With Too Much Talking
lectures.description: In our Monday Night Mishlei shiur (3/15/21 with Lomdeha, hosted by YBT) we learned a pasuk which seemed like a cliche Mishlei idea at first glance. As always, once we delved into the analysis, we became sensitive to the nuances and we managed to uncover a new idea. As usual, we also discussed a lot of methodology along the way.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Torah vs. Heresy #20: Lady Wisdom's Warm Invitation - Mishlei 9:1-12
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Aron Zimmer

lectures.title: Mishlei 19:21 - Man's Plans vs. Hashem's Advice (Part 2)
lectures.description: This morning (3/11/21 at YBT) we learned the Ralbag on yesterday's pasuk, which helped us clarify Mishlei's treatment of the subject of hashgachah. And as an aside, I am pleased to announce that this is the 100th Mishlei shiur I've given at YBT this year. Here's to the next 100, בג"ה!
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 19:21 - Man's Plans vs. Hashem's Advice (Part 1)
lectures.description: This morning (3/10/21 at YBT) we learned a pasuk that many of us say every day as part of davening. The challenge with such familiar pesukim is to be able to look at them with fresh eyes. I believe we succeeded in that this morning, and developed some nice approaches which we will continue to explore tomorrow.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 19:20 - Mussar Now, Chochmah Later (Part 2)
lectures.description: This morning (3/9/21 at YBT) we learned the meforshim on yesterday's pasuk, after reviewing and developing what we came up with yesterday. Rabbeinu Yonah and Metzudas David took opposite approaches, each with its own advantages.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 10:18 - How NOT to Deal with Hatred
lectures.description: In our Monday Night Mishlei shiur (3/8/21 with Lomdeha, hosted by YBT) we learned a pasuk which leant itself to several different readings. Thankfully, the several streams of thought in the group flowed into a single river, and we arrived at a consensus about the main idea - one which highlighted Mishlei's intended role as a commentary on Torah.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 19:20 - Mussar Now, Chochmah Later (Part 1)
lectures.description: This morning (3/8/21 at YBT) we learned a pasuk that was complex in its simplicity: easy to translate, but broad and obvious-sounding enough that it posed some difficulty. We worked out a general approach which we hope to flesh out tomorrow with the aid of the meforshim.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Torah vs. Heresy #19: Wisdom's Central Role in Reality - Mishlei 8:14-36
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Aron Zimmer

lectures.title: Mishlei 19:19 - The Inescapable Punishment of Great Wrath (Part 2)
lectures.description: This morning (3/4/21 at YBT) we continued our analysis of yesterday's pasuk - this time, with help from the meforshim! Rabbeinu Yonah connected 19:19 with 19:18, taking a similar route to Rashi, but with greater elaboration and broader implications. Metzudas David was more difficult to understand, but led to a good discussion. We took a quick look at the (fake) Ibn Ezra at the end of shiur, who took a creative approach to this pasuk.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 19:19 - The Inescapable Punishment of Great Wrath (Part 1)
lectures.description: This morning (3/3/21 at YBT) we began a pasuk which was REALLY challenging to translate! We began with a summary of the Abravanel's view of kri/ksiv, then we did the messy work of translating the pasuk, and we concluded by raising major questions and problems, and venturing one possible approach to the pasuk. Hopefully the meforshim will help us out tomorrow.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 19:18 - Rationalizations for Not Giving Mussar (Part 2)
lectures.description: This morning (3/2/21 at YBT) we continued the pasuk we began yesterday. We started with Rabbeinu Yonah, whose explanation was the closest to the approach we took yesterday. We then contrasted this with Rashi's explanation of the second half, which was almost the opposite. This led to a discussion about corporal punishment in general. We ended by comparing and contrasting Rabbeinu Yonah's and Rashi's explanations of the pasuk.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 10:17 - Guarding Mussar vs. Abandoning Tochachah
lectures.description: In our Monday Night Mishlei shiur (3/1/21 with Lomdeha, hosted by YBT) we faced another formidable pasuk, with many possible readings. Our discussions in shiur are often unpredictable. This time, instead of trying out many approaches that were clearly demarcated, we ended up proceeding seemlessly from one approach to the other without even realizing it. We attempted to summarize our three main approaches in the end, which I hope made things clearer!
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 19:18 - Rationalizations for Not Giving Mussar (Part 1)
lectures.description: Sometimes it's the straightforward-sounding pesukim that are the most difficult to understand. This morning (3/1/21 at YBT) we read a fairly straightforward pasuk addressing a father's rationalizations for not disciplining his son. Perhaps it's because this pasuk can be taken in different directions, and perhaps it's because the topic of rebuke is very broad, but either way, we ended the day feeling like we were at a bit of a crossroads. Tomorrow we'll turn to the meforshim for guidance.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 19:17 - Lending to Hashem (Part 2)
lectures.description: This morning (2/24/21 at YBT) we revisited and refined our idea from last time using a surprising source: the Rambam in the Peirush ha'Mishnayos to Peah 1:1. Then, in another shocking move, we tried our hand at understanding Rashi's interpretation, which was echoed by the Ri Nachmias. If you're looking for an idea to pair with your matanos la'evyonim this Purim, be sure to check this out!
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 10:16 - The Systemic Ripple Effects of the Tzadik and the Rasha
lectures.description: In our Monday Night Mishlei shiur (2/22/21 with Lomdeha, hosted by YBT) we learned a pasuk which, like many pesukim in Mishlei, focused on the difference between a tzadik and a rasha. We ended up DEFINING the terms "tzadik" and "rasha," based on my understanding of how they're used in Mishlei, and explaning the pasuk on that basis.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 19:17 - Lending to Hashem (Part 1)
lectures.description: This morning (2/22/21 at YBT) we learned a difficult pasuk with a seemingly inappropriate metaphor. We struggled to figure out an approach, turned to Rabbeinu Yonah for guidance, and then proposed an explanation. We'll revisit this pasuk tomorrow to see if we can refine today's idea, and to see what the other meforshim have to say.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Torah vs. Heresy #18: Lady Wisdom's New Speech - Mishlei 8:1-13
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Aron Zimmer

lectures.title: Mishlei 19:16 - Three Attitudes Towards Mitzvos (and Masks)
lectures.description: This morning (2/18/20 at YBT) we learned a pasuk that seemed ambiguous on multiple levels, but we found that "all rivers run into the sea" (i.e. all of the translation permutations led to the same basic idea). This isn't the first time I've encountered a pasuk like that, and I don't know what to make of it, other than to note that it is noteworthy.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 19:15 - Stomach Gasses and Guaranteed Poverty
lectures.description: This morning (2/17/20 at YBT) we consulted the meforshim on the pasuk we learned yesterday. We began with Saadia Gaon's commentary (as presented by the Meiri), then learned the Meiri's own interpretation, and concluded with Rabbeinu Yonah's explanation. We also read Rashi, but didn't have time to figure out what he was saying.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 19:15 - Are You Tired and Hungry or Just Lazy?
lectures.description: This morning (2/16/20 at YBT) we starting learning a pasuk about laziness. Knowing my fondness for Saadia Gaon's definition of laziness as stated in his Introduction to Mishlei, it was inevitable that we'd end up there. Thankfully, we were able to work out an idea combining that definition of laziness with his translation of "remiyah" here. Tomorrow we'll look at the other meforshim.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 10:15 - The Self-Perpetuating Psychological Impact of Wealth and Poverty
lectures.description: In our Monday Night Mishlei shiur (2/15/21 with Lomdeha, hosted by YBT) we tackled a pasuk that was mystifying in some ways and obvious in others. We discussed a LOT of methodology, both during and after shiur, including topics such as the difference between Mishlei and Pirkei Avos, the caution needed when attempting to interpret pesukim in a more universal manner than the words suggest, the subtle differences between interpretation and application, and more. Oh, and did I mention we also came up with several interpretations of the actual pasuk which were reflected in the meforshim? Suffice it to say, this was a jam-packed shiur.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 19:14 - An Intelligent Wife is From Hashem
lectures.description: The last pasuk we learned was about a contentious wife, and the pasuk we learned this morning (2/15/20 at YBT) was about an intelligent wife. This was one of those pesukim that was unclear on a number of levels: what it means, who it's for, and what are its implications. We came up with our own approach, found value in the Meiri's nigleh and nistar interpretations, and were puzzled by Rabbeinu Yonah.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Torah vs. Heresy #17: The Heretical Seductress in the Night of Exile - Mishlei 7:1-27
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Aron Zimmer

lectures.title: Mishlei 19:13 - Foolish Sons and Nagging Wives (Part 2)
lectures.description: This morning (2/11/20 at YBT) we continued our analysis of yesterday's pasuk about the negative impact of foolish sons and nagging wives. We learned Rabbeinu Yonah and the Meiri, then compared and contrasted the two interpretations, with a few observations of our own. We concluded by reading the Meiri's "derech nistar" approach, but didn't have time to work on it.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 19:13 - Foolish Sons and Nagging Wives (Part 1)
lectures.description: This morning (2/10/20 at YBT) we began a pasuk about the negative impact of foolish sons and nagging wives. Since we had 30 minutes instead of the usual 45, we only had time to raise the questions and begin developing an approach. Tomorrow (בג"ה) we'll develop our approach and consult the meforshim.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 19:12 - The Roar and Dew of the King of the Universe
lectures.description: This morning (2/9/20 at YBT) we continued our analysis of yesterday's pasuk. First we reviewed the idea from Rabbeinu Yonah, then we compared it to the Metzudas David, and then we did something we usually don't do: we attempted to understand Rashi's interpretation, with help and guidance from the Meiri.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 10:14 - A Mishleic Take on the Rhetorical Triangle
lectures.description: In our Monday Night Mishlei shiur (2/8/21 with Lomdeha, hosted by YBT) we learned yet another pasuk about chachamim, fools, and speech. Our analysis was an exercise in balancing our understanding of terms based on previous pesukim with keeping our minds open to new interpretations. We ultimately arrived at one clear idea and a few ideas that still could use some work.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 19:12 - The Silent Roar and Loud Dew of a King
lectures.description: MORNING MISHLEI IS BACK, BABY! The pasuk we learned this morning (2/8/20 at YBT) features a bizarrely asymmetrical metaphor whose meaning and practical import is not at all clear. We spent the morning experimenting with various approaches and concluded with (what I consider to be) the most viable approach among the meforshim, that of Rabbeinu Yonah. Tomorrow we'll revisit this pasuk and attempt to sharpen our understanding, and maybe take a look at some other meforshim as well.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 10:13 - The Crossroads on the Path to Becoming a Creative Thinker
lectures.description: In our Monday Night Mishlei shiur (2/1/21 with Lomdeha, hosted by YBT, broadcasting from Seattle due to a snow storm in NY) we learned one of those pesukim in which the two halves seem to have nothing to do with each other. On top of that, the pasuk contained technical jargon of the most difficult variety: "knowledge words" (i.e. navon, chochmah, chasar leiv). And yet, with our usual Monday Night Mishlei teamwork, we were able to arrive at several nice ideas, with a lot of methodology along the way. And in a way, our pasuk was about methodology and the type of courage it takes to make progress in one's development as a thinker.
lectures.speaker: Rabbi Matthew Schneeweiss

lectures.title: Mishlei 10:13 - The Crossroads on the Path to Becoming a Creative Thinker
